questions.stem: What is a database, in the simplest definition?
options: A dimensional model of business facts
A medium to store structured data
A tool for scraping websites
A network of servers rented from a cloud vendor
A report produced for decision makers
questions.explanation: A database is defined as a medium to store structured data; it is a datastore, not a data modelling solution.

questions.stem: Why can a database not be linked to any one data modelling solution?
options: Because databases only support NoSQL models
Because OLTP, data warehouses, data marts and OLAP all use databases as the medium to store their data sets
Because databases cannot store relations
Because data models are stored on tape drives
Because databases predate data modelling
questions.explanation: A database is a datastore: OLTP, data warehouse, data mart and OLAP solutions all use databases as their storage medium, so the database itself is not tied to one modelling approach.

questions.stem: What does OLTP (Online Transaction Processing) do?
options: Stores pre-aggregated cubes for analysis
Stores business transactions in real time with insert, update and delete capability and the ACID feature
Archives historical data on tape drives
Virtualises data from multiple sources
Extracts data from web pages
questions.explanation: OLTP stores business transactions in real time with insert, update and delete capability and the ACID feature; it is the oldest and most used medium in every era.

questions.stem: Under which term do data warehouses and data marts normally fall?
options: OLTP (Online Transactional Processing)
OLAP (Online Analytical Processing)
NoSQL
Big Data
Data virtualization
questions.explanation: Databases are normally called OLTP, whereas data warehouses and data marts fall under the term OLAP.

questions.stem: Which statement about Big Data and Data Lakes in relation to OLTP and OLAP is correct?
options: They are firmly classified as OLTP
They are firmly classified as OLAP
The data world has yet to tag them as OLTP or OLAP, but they are certainly not meant for OLTP
They replace both OLTP and OLAP
They are classified as RDBMS
questions.explanation: Big Data and Data Lakes have not yet been tagged as OLTP or OLAP, but they are certainly not meant for OLTP; meanwhile NoSQL is stepping into the OLTP zone.

questions.stem: Why are databases called RDBMS (relational database management systems)?
options: Because they store data on related servers
Because data in tables can be joined with each other using relations
Because they are related to a data warehouse
Because every table has a relation to a tape backup
Because they relate to real-time reporting
questions.explanation: In databases there are tables, rows and columns, and data in tables can be joined using relations, which is why they are called relational database management systems.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the normalisation concept in the OLTP world?
options: To speed up reporting queries
To make sure there is no duplication of data
To pre-aggregate KPIs
To encrypt sensitive columns
To convert NoSQL data into tables
questions.explanation: In OLTP, normalisation makes sure there is no duplication of data; most data models are normalised up to 3NF.

questions.stem: In Third Normal Form (3NF), data modellers keep breaking tables until what condition is met?
options: Every table has fewer than ten columns
All non-key columns are dependent on key columns
All tables fit on a single tape drive
Every table has a foreign key to a fact table
No table contains more than one row per customer
questions.explanation: In 3NF, data modellers keep breaking tables down until all the non-key columns are dependent on key columns.

questions.stem: Before the 1990s, why did organisations offload OLTP data to tape drives, and what challenge did this bring?
options: Storage and processing were expensive; it created a challenge in decision-making on historical data
Tape was faster than disk; it created a challenge of duplicate records
Regulators required it; it created a challenge of data sovereignty
Databases could not store text; it created a challenge of encoding
Networks were unreliable; it created a challenge of table locking
questions.explanation: Storage and processing power were a big challenge and expensive, so data was offloaded to tape, which made decision-making on historical data difficult.

questions.stem: Why did the normalised (3NF) extraction copy of OLTP become a bottleneck for decision-support queries?
options: Because it could not store more than a few KPIs
Because queries had to join tens or hundreds of tables, slowing a single query from minutes to 10–20 hours
Because table locking prevented any reads
Because it was stored on tape
Because it lacked the ACID feature
questions.explanation: With tables broken down in 3NF, extraction queries had to search tens or hundreds of tables using joins, slowing a query from minutes to 10–20 hours; Bill Inmon's data warehouse was proposed to mitigate this.
